Modules (id, code, uri, name, credits, compulsory): 6833502 FI1 moduulikoodistolops2021_fi1 'Johdatus filosofiseen ajatteluun' 2 op pakollinen=true; 6833503 FI2 ..._fi2 'Etiikka' (name has a trailing space in the API) 2 op true; 6833504 FI3 ..._fi3 'Yhteiskuntafilosofia' 2 op false; 6833505 FI4 ..._fi4 'Totuus' 2 op false.

Counts for a fetcher check (objectives / content items; each module has exactly 1 sisallot area with null name and kuvaus): FI1 5/5; FI2 6/6; FI3 5/6; FI4 6/7. Totals 22 objectives and 24 content items. Subject-level objectives: 6, in one tavoitealue 'Filosofian opetuksen tavoitteena on, että' with kohde 'opiskelija'.

FI1 objectives (stem: 'Moduulin tavoitteena on, että opiskelija'): T1 [9563458] muodostaa käsityksen filosofian luonteesta ja menetelmistä tutustumalla filosofisiin ongelmiin ja niiden mahdollisiin ratkaisuihin; T2 [9563459] oppii arvioimaan väitteiden totuutta sekä harjaantuu esittämään ja vaatimaan erilaisille väitteille perusteluja, hahmottamaan perustelujen rakennetta sekä arvioimaan niiden pätevyyttä; T3 [9563460] tuntee ja oppii erilaisten vuorovaikutteisten harjoitusten ja keskustelujen kautta soveltamaan filosofian työtapoja, kuten oletusten kyseenalaistamista, käsitteiden luokittelua ja määrittelemistä sekä ajatuskokeiden ja vastaesimerkkien käyttöä; T4 [9563461] perehtyy joihinkin keskeisiin filosofisiin kysymyksiin ja niihin liittyviin käsitteellisiin erotteluihin; T5 [9563462] osaa eritellä ja arvioida kriittisesti erilaisia tiedollisia uskomuksia ja tutustuu tietämiseen joissain lukion oppiaineissa.

FI1 content items: S1 [9563466] mitä filosofia on, filosofinen kysymyksenasettelu sekä ajattelu filosofian perinteessä ja ajankohtaisissa aiheissa; S2 [9563470] johdonmukaisen argumentaation ja pätevän päättelyn perusteet sekä niiden harjoitteleminen suullisesti ja kirjallisesti, muun muassa ajankohtaisiin yhteiskunnallisiin ongelmiin sovellettuna; S3 [9563471] keskeisiä filosofisia peruskysymyksiä ja -erotteluja: henki ja aine, vapaus ja välttämättömyys, käsitteellinen ja empiirinen, objektiivinen ja subjektiivinen; S4 [9563472] tiedon ja informaation, arkitiedon ja tieteellisen tiedon sekä tieteen ja pseudotieteen ero; S5 [9563473] tiedon ja argumentaation luonne eri tiedonaloilla: miten väitteitä muodostetaan, koetellaan ja perustellaan joissain lukion oppiaineissa.

FI2 Etiikka objectives (stem same): T1 [9563478] perehtyy filosofisen etiikan keskeisiin käsitteisiin, kysymyksiin ja teorioihin; T2 [9563479] osaa perustella käsityksiä hyvästä ja oikeasta sekä hahmottaa normatiivisten ja kuvailevien väitteiden eron; T3 [9563480] osaa esittää suullisesti ja kirjallisesti johdonmukaisia eettisiä argumentteja sekä perustella moraalin velvoittavuutta; T4 [9563481] oppii jäsentämään oman elämänsä merkityksellisyyttä ja elämänvalintojaan filosofisen käsitteistön avulla; T5 [9563482] osaa eritellä ja arvioida toimintaa eettisesti sekä kykenee jäsentämään omia moraalisia ratkaisujaan ja arvioitaan filosofisen etiikan välinein; T6 [9563483] osaa soveltaa etiikkaa yhteiskuntaa ja ympäristöä koskeviin kysymyksiin.

FI2 content: S1 [9563487] moraalin luonne normijärjestelmänä; moraalin, lakien ja tapojen ero; moraalinen objektivismi, relativismi, subjektivismi; S2 [9563488] moraalia tarkasteleva normatiivinen ja soveltava etiikka; hyveet, seuraukset, oikeudet ja velvollisuudet; S3 [9563489] filosofisia teorioita elämän hyvyydestä ja merkityksellisyydestä sekä hyvästä elämäntavasta; S4 [9563490] etiikka ja yksilön moraaliset ratkaisut: ihmissuhteet ja elämänvalinnat; S5 [9563491] ympäristöä ja luontoa koskevia eettisiä kysymyksiä, kuten ilmastonmuutos ja eläinten oikeudet; S6 [9563492] etiikka ja yhteiskunta: ihmis- ja perusoikeudet.

FI3 Yhteiskuntafilosofia objectives: T1 [9563497] perehtyy joihinkin yhteiskuntafilosofian keskeisiin käsitteisiin ja suuntauksiin; T2 [9563498] oppii erittelemään oikeudenmukaisuutta, vapautta, tasa-arvoa ja vallankäyttöä yksilöiden, yhteisöjen ja instituutioiden toiminnassa; T3 [9563499] pystyy arvioimaan filosofisesti yhteiskunnan rakennetta ja sen oikeutusta; T4 [9563500] osaa soveltaa oppimaansa ajankohtaisiin yhteiskunnallisiin kysymyksiin; T5 [9563501] ymmärtää oikeuksien merkityksen yhteiskunnan perustana. Content: S1 [9563505] yhteiskuntajärjestyksen oikeuttaminen, yhteiskuntasopimusteoriat; S2 [9563506] vallan, vapauden, tasa-arvon ja oikeudenmukaisuuden eri muodot; S3 [9563507] ihmisoikeudet, kansalaisoikeudet ja oikeusvaltio; demokratia ja yhteisöllisyys yhteiskunnallisina arvoina; S4 [9563508] poliittiset ihanteet: liberalismi, sosialismi, anarkismi, konservatismi, nationalismi; yhteiskunnalliset utopiat ja dystopiat; S5 [9563509] hyvinvoinnin ja talouden suhde; tulo-, varallisuus- ja hyvinvointierojen oikeuttaminen; hyvinvointivaltio; S6 [9563510] ajankohtaisia yhteiskuntafilosofisia kysymyksiä: ympäristöongelmat, kulttuurien kohtaaminen, teknologian ja tekoälyn vaikutukset, sukupuoli ja valta, eriarvoistavien rakenteiden tunnistaminen ja kritiikki.

FI4 Totuus objectives: T1 [9563515] osaa erottaa mielipiteet tosiasiaväittämistä ja ymmärtää tarpeen perustella tosiasiaväittämät; T2 [9563516] ymmärtää kielen ja merkitysten roolin todellisuuden hahmottamisessa; T3 [9563517] osaa eritellä ja arvioida filosofisia teorioita totuudesta, tiedosta, todellisuuden luonteesta ja tieteestä; T4 [9563518] osaa jäsentää ja eritellä tieteellisen tutkimuksen, päättelyn ja selittämisen luonnetta; T5 [9563519] osaa arvioida havainnon ja tiedon sekä tieteellisten teorioiden suhdetta totuuteen; T6 [9563520] oppii arvioimaan tilanteita, joissa eri tutkimukset antavat erilaisia tuloksia ja toimintavaihtoehtoja. Content: S1 [9563524] kieli, merkitys ja totuus; S2 [9563525] totuuden luonne ja totuusteoriat; totuuden lähestyminen; välttämätön ja kontingentti totuus; S3 [9563526] todellisuuden ja tietoisuuden luonne; realismi ja antirealismi; S4 [9563527] tiedon lähteet, tiedon mahdollisuus ja rajat, tiedon oikeuttaminen, tiedon suhde varmuuteen; S5 [9563528] tieteellisen tutkimuksen luonne ja menetelmiä sekä tieteellinen päättely; tieteen etiikka; S6 [9563529] tieteen menetelmien ja teorioiden luotettavuus ja suhde todellisuuteen; S7 [9563530] selittäminen, ennustaminen, ymmärtäminen ja tulkinta erilaisissa tieteissä.

Subject general objectives, 'Filosofian opetuksen tavoitteena on, että opiskelija' (6): [9563437] osaa hahmottaa filosofisia ongelmia sekä niiden erilaisia mahdollisia ratkaisuja filosofian perinteessä ja ajankohtaisiin kysymyksiin sovellettuina; [9563438] osaa käsitteellisesti eritellä, jäsentää ja arvioida informaatiota, erityisesti erilaisia väitteitä, niiden merkityksiä ja perusteluja; [9563439] hallitsee johdonmukaisen argumentaation perustaidot, mikä auttaa kehittämään omaa ajattelua, arvioimaan sitä kriittisesti sekä pohtimaan sen rajoja eri tieteenaloilla ja arkielämässä; [9563440] kykenee arvioimaan moraalisia ongelmia ja niiden mahdollisia ratkaisuja sekä sitoutumaan eettisiin periaatteisiin; [9563441] oppii pohtimaan ja jäsentämään käsitteellisesti laajoja kokonaisuuksia sekä ajattelemaan ja toimimaan arvostelukykyisesti niin eettisissä kysymyksissä kuin muillakin elämänalueilla myös informaation ollessa epävarmaa tai ristiriitaista; [9563442] kehittää kykyään ilmaista näkemyksiään järkiperäisesti perustellen.

Subject task (tehtava.kuvaus, one long text, no heading): philosophy examines all of reality and ways of grasping it; trains weighing justifications; helps sort information overload and separate factual statements from opinions; 'mother of all sciences' so integrates fields; strengthens identity and ethical reflection; students learn to form and justify own views while respecting differing justified views; dialogical working methods suit the subject. Starts 'Filosofia tarkastelee koko todellisuutta ja eri tapoja hahmottaa sitä.'

Assessment (arviointi.kuvaus): targets understanding of central philosophical questions, mastery of thinking skills and concepts, and ability to express and evaluate philosophical thinking; conceptual clarification of information; spotting philosophical problems in daily life and science and formulating them; knowing proposed solutions; consistent arguments in writing, speech and interaction; supports self-reflection and planning of own study; varied methods; general objectives are assessed 'moduulikohtaisten tavoitteiden ja keskeisten sisältöjen kautta'. No numeric grading scale or per-module assessment text is in the oppiaine object.

Transversal competences (laajaAlaisetOsaamiset.kuvaus, one text, no per-competence ids): covers vuorovaikutusosaaminen, hyvinvointiosaaminen (understanding self, virtues, tolerating uncertainty), monitieteinen ja luova osaaminen, yhteiskunnallinen osaaminen (rational ethics based on democracy, human rights, sustainable future), eettisyys and ympäristöosaaminen, globaali- ja kulttuuriosaaminen (ethics and social philosophy; thought experiments as futures thinking). Source text has a typo 'Gloabaali-'.

FI1 in plain words: students get a picture of what philosophy is and how it works by meeting real philosophical problems and possible answers; practise giving and demanding reasons, seeing how arguments are built and judging whether they are valid; learn the working methods (questioning assumptions, classifying and defining concepts, thought experiments, counterexamples) through interactive exercises and discussions; meet a few central questions and conceptual distinctions (mind and matter, freedom and necessity, conceptual and empirical, objective and subjective); critically analyse beliefs and see how knowing works in some other lukio subjects (knowledge vs information, everyday vs scientific knowledge, science vs pseudoscience). Argument skills are practised orally and in writing, including on current social problems. It names no specific philosophers, works or texts, so primary texts are the site's own choice, not a curriculum requirement.

recommendations: Name FI4 'Totuus' in all site files and briefs; correct the brief's expected answer, which said 'Tieto, tiede ja todellisuus'.

Use ePerusteet content ids (for example 9563458 for FI1 T1, 9563466 for FI1 S1) as the stable curriculum codes. The fetcher check is 5/5 (FI1), 6/6 (FI2), 5/6 (FI3), 6/7 (FI4) objectives/content items, 22 and 24 in total. Number items by array order (T1.., S1..) and keep the ids beside them.

Do not claim the curriculum requires any named philosopher or text. FI1 S3 names four distinctions (henki ja aine, vapaus ja välttämättömyys, käsitteellinen ja empiirinen, objektiivinen ja subjektiivinen); give each a topic. FI1 T5 and S5 require links to other lukio subjects, so plan at least one cross-subject topic and a pseudoscience topic (S4).
Quote Finnish wording exactly from the API, including the FI2 trailing space in the name (trim it on import) and the source typo 'Gloabaali-' (do not copy it).
Re-fetch the API before the build brief, because muokattu and julkaisu timestamps show the peruste was updated in 2026; store the fetch date. Use curl, as WebFetch truncates the 4 MB JSON.
Do not copy the full curriculum prose into the site; cite ids and short phrases only, and link ePerusteet as the source.
research.versus_expected: Mostly right: FI1 Johdatus filosofiseen ajatteluun and FI2 Etiikka are compulsory at 2 op, FI3 Yhteiskuntafilosofia and FI4 are national optional at 2 op, and FI1 covers the nature of philosophy, argumentation, concept analysis and some questions in knowledge and metaphysics. Wrong or refined: (1) FI4 is named 'Totuus', not 'Tieto, tiede ja todellisuus'. (2) FI1 does not contain ethics; ethics is FI2. FI1 covers epistemology (knowledge versus information, science versus pseudoscience) and four basic distinctions, one of them mind and matter (metaphysics). (3) The API gives no grading scale or matriculation-exam information, so '4-10' and the exam claim are not checked here and remain unverified. (4) Subject-level objectives number 6 and assessment is a single text, not per module. (5) The curriculum names no philosophers or texts, so every primary-text choice is the site's own."

research.summary: Primary-texts scout, read-only. Opened about 30 URLs. Verified working originals: Perseus Greek Plato (Apology 38a, Republic 514a via a page= URL) and Aristotle Metaphysics (982b, 1011b); Latin Wikisource Descartes Meditationes (Adam-Tannery with AT page numbers); German Wikisource Kant "Was ist Aufklärung?" (Berlinische Monatsschrift 1784); Greek Wikisource Epictetus Enchiridion and Epicurus Letter to Menoeceus; Latin Library Seneca index; French Wikisource Rousseau Contrat social (1762); English Wikisource Hume Enquiry (1748) and Hobbes Leviathan (1651 Head edition); Internet Archive German Kant Grundlegung (Kirchmann 1870). Not confirmed: Project Gutenberg (503 on every fetch), the Perseus NE URL, a clean German Tractatus, and Mill Utilitarianism on Wikisource. Perseus URLs are fragile: guessed IDs or section keys redirect to invalidquery.jsp. Perseus shows English (Loeb) by default for some IDs, and the Loeb translations are not PD-safe to copy. Death years and licence status below are from model knowledge unless stated, and need a quick source check before the build.

findings.claim: FI1 area 'what philosophy is, wonder': Aristotle Metaphysics A.2, Bekker 982b (wonder as origin of philosophy). Aristotle d. 322 BC, PD. Opened Perseus page for book 1 section 982b: the page lists the Greek (1924, Ross) beside the Loeb English (Tredennick). Open URL: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0052:book=1:section=982b (Perseus ID 0051 is the Greek, 0052 the English). Reference: Bekker numbers plus book and chapter.

Plato Theaetetus 155d (wonder as the beginning of philosophy). Plato d. 347 BC, PD. The Perseus page opens and shows Fowler's Loeb English (1921) with a link to the Greek (1903, Burnet). Greek-by-default URL not confirmed. Stephanus numbering. Page: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0172:text=Theaet.:section=155d . Wording 'Tht.' in the section key fails (redirects to invalidquery); use 'Theaet.'.

Plato Apology 38a ('the unexamined life is not worth living'): Greek Burnet (OUP 1903) is displayed at https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0169:text=Apol.:section=38a . The page returned the phrase 'ὁ δὲ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ'. Stephanus 38a. ID 0170 gives Fowler's English. Serves 'what philosophy is' and the Socratic method.

Plato Republic 514a (cave) opens in Greek (Burnet 1903) at https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0167:book=7:page=514 ; the opening reads 'μετὰ ταῦτα δή, εἶπον, ἀπείκασον'. Use book plus page=NNN URLs for the Republic. The section=514a form returns only a table of contents, and the 'Rep.' text-key form redirects to invalidquery. Stephanus 514a-517a. The same passage serves metaphysics and epistemology.

Plato Meno 80d (Meno's paradox, inquiry into the unknown) opens at https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0178:text=Meno:section=80d . It shows Lamb's Loeb English (1967) with the Greek (1903) behind a toggle. Meno 80d-86c also covers definition and recollection. The Greek-by-default ID was not determined. Plato d. 347 BC, PD.

Aristotle Metaphysics Gamma 1011b (the definition of truth, 'to say of what is that it is'): Greek, Ross 1924 text, opens at https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0051:book=4:section=1011b . The page shows truth and falsity in terms of being and non-being. Bekker 1011b25 is the standard citation.

Descartes Meditationes de prima philosophia, I-II (doubt, cogito): Latin Wikisource has the Adam-Tannery text (Paris 1897-1910) at https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/Meditationes_de_prima_philosophia_(Adam_et_Tannery) . Contents: Epistola, Praefatio, Synopsis, Meditatio I-VI. The Meditatio II subpage opens 'In tantas dubitationes hesternâ meditatione conjectus sum' and marks AT pages inline ([25] to [34]), so AT volume VII page citation is possible. A 1685 Amsterdam edition is also listed. Descartes d. 1650, PD. The disambiguation page https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/Meditationes_de_prima_philosophia has no text of its own.

Hume, Enquiry Sections IV (sceptical doubts) and XII (sceptical philosophy): English Wikisource has the 1748 Millar first edition (Philosophical Essays) at https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/An_Enquiry_Concerning_Human_Understanding . Essay IV is on p. 47 and Essay XII on p. 232 of that edition; the page notes the Internet Archive scan 'humehumanunderstanding'. Hume d. 1776, PD. The SBN reference system (Selby-Bigge/Nidditch) is a modern pagination and is not shown on this page, so section numbers are the safe citation (SBN is unconfirmed).

Epictetus Enchiridion 1 ('some things are up to us'): Greek Wikisource page https://el.wikisource.org/wiki/Ἐγχειρίδιον has 53 chapters, and chapter 1 opens 'Τῶν ὄντων τὰ μέν ἐστιν ἐφ' ἡμῖν'. The page names no critical edition, so the original is linked as a Wikisource transcription of unnamed provenance. Epictetus d. c. AD 135 (year approximate), PD. Chapter numbers are the reference system. Useful for free will, the good life and Stoic ethics.

Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus: Greek Wikisource page https://el.wikisource.org/wiki/Επιστολή_προς_Μενοικέα (opens 'Ἐπίκουρος Μενοικεῖ χαίρειν'), CC BY-SA 4.0 per the page, with no printed edition named. The text is transmitted in Diogenes Laertius X, 122-135, which is the standard citation. Epicurus d. 270 BC, PD. Useful for the good life and a first look at ethics.

Kant, 'Beantwortung der Frage: Was ist Aufklärung?': German Wikisource page https://de.wikisource.org/wiki/Beantwortung_der_Frage:_Was_ist_Aufkl%C3%A4rung%3F transcribes Berlinische Monatsschrift vol. 4, Dec. 1784, pp. 481-494 (scan from UB Bielefeld). It opens 'Aufklärung ist der Ausgang des Menschen aus seiner selbst verschuldeten Unmündigkeit'. No Akademie-Ausgabe pagination (AA VIII, 33-42) appears on the page, so the Akademie pages must be added from another source. Kant d. 1804, PD.

Kant, Grundlegung zur Metaphysik der Sitten (FI2): German Wikisource has no page of its own, because the exact title does not exist there. A usable open original is the Internet Archive OCR of Kirchmann's 1870 Heimann edition: https://archive.org/stream/immanuelkantsgru00kant/immanuelkantsgru00kant_djvu.txt (German, text OCR, about 918,000 characters). The first edition is Riga: Hartknoch 1785. Citation by Akademie page (AA IV) or by 1785 pagination is not shown on that scan. Kant d. 1804, PD. German Wikisource's Immanuel Kant page was reported to link e-texts, but I did not open it.

Seneca, Epistulae morales: the Latin Library index https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/sen.html lists Liber I to XX. The guessed URL .../seneca/sen.ep1.shtml returned 404, so I did not open an individual letter, and the exact subpage URL needs one more check. A York University page also has the Latin of Book I (https://www.yorku.ca/pswarney/Texts/seneca/epistula/epistula-1.htm, search-reported only). Seneca d. AD 65, PD. Reference: letter and section (Ep. 1, De brevitate vitae). Good for Stoic ethics, time and the good life.

Hobbes, Leviathan (FI3): English Wikisource https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Leviathan_(Hobbes) transcribes the 1651 'Head' edition (Andrew Crooke) from an Internet Archive PDF; ch. XIII (p. 60) and ch. XIV (p. 64) are linked. Hobbes d. 1679, PD. Reference: chapter and the 1651 page number.

Rousseau, Du contrat social (FI3): French Wikisource has the 1762 Rey edition (https://fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Du_contrat_social/Édition_1762, full text at .../Texte_entier, search-reported) and the Beaulavon 1903 edition with commentary. The title I guessed, Du_contrat_social_(1762), returned 404. I read only the search result list, not the text pages. Rousseau d. 1778, PD. Reference: book and chapter.

Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) (FI3): the English Wikisource page https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Vindication_of_the_Rights_of_Woman exists (the fetch returned only an encyclopaedic summary). Wollstonecraft d. 1797, PD. Edition and chapter structure were not read.

Wittgenstein, Tractatus (d. 1951, PD in the EU from 1 Jan 2022 on the life+70 rule): German Wikisource has no Tractatus page (search found none). A German PDF exists at the Wittgenstein Project (https://books.wittgensteinproject.org/pdf/german/Logisch-philosophische%20Abhandlung.pdf, 850 KB) but its contents could not be read (compressed PDF, edition unconfirmed). The 1922 Ogden/Ramsey English is not PD in the EU (Ogden d. 1957, so 2028), so only the German original can be quoted. Numbered propositions (1, 1.1 ...) are the reference system. Unverified for source quality.

Perseus URL behaviour: wrong IDs or section keys redirect to invalidquery.jsp. The Greek and English IDs differ by one (Apology 0169/0170, Metaphysics 0051/0052). Perseus shows the Loeb English by default on some IDs (Fowler 1921, Lamb 1967, Tredennick 1933/1989), and those translations are not for the site to copy. Whether the Greek loads by default depends on the ID. Lamb d. 1949 and Fowler d. 1955 are PD in the EU, but the Loeb Tredennick is not. Link out only.

Death years and PD status stated from model knowledge, not read on a page: Plato 347 BC; Aristotle 322 BC; Epicurus 270 BC; Seneca AD 65; Epictetus c. AD 135; Descartes 1650; Hobbes 1679; Locke 1704; Hume 1776; Rousseau 1778; Wollstonecraft 1797; Kant 1804; Hegel 1831; Bentham 1832; Mill 1873; Wittgenstein 1951. All are well past the 70-year rule in Finland and the EU. Only the Hume Wikisource page stated the PD status in text. Popper d. 1994 and Russell d. 1970 are not PD and may only be paraphrased.

Planned passage map by FI1 area (not all opened): argument, validity, fallacies has no single classic passage; use Aristotle Prior Analytics 24b18 / Sophistical Refutations 164a and Plato Euthydemus (unopened, unverified). Concept analysis: Plato Meno 71e-77a, Euthyphro 6d-e, Theaetetus 146c-e (unopened). Socratic method: Apology 21a-23b and 38a, Meno 80d-86c, Republic book 1 (partly opened). Metaphysics and mind: Descartes Med. II and VI, Plato Phaedo 78b-84b (unopened). Free will: Epictetus Ench. 1, Aristotle NE III 1110a-1111b (unopened), Hume Enquiry VIII. Epistemology: Plato Theaetetus 151e, Descartes Med. I, Locke Essay II.1 (unopened), Hume Enquiry IV and XII. Ethics: Epicurus Menoeceus, Aristotle NE I 1094a / 1098a, Seneca De brevitate vitae.

Project Gutenberg returned HTTP 503 (Retry-After 21600) on the two ebooks pages and the 9662 HTML I tried. Locke Essay II.1, Mill, Bentham, Wollstonecraft and Hume on Gutenberg could therefore not be checked. Wikisource and the Internet Archive were the working alternatives. The English Wikisource Mill page Utilitarianism_(Mill) was 404. Index:Enquiry_..._(1748).djvu was also 404, though the main Hume page works.

recommendations: Store each original as a stable-URL tuple (work, author, edition named on the page, passage reference, URL, read date). Prefer Perseus Greek IDs 0169 (Apology), 0167 (Republic) and 0051 (Metaphysics), la.wikisource AT pages, de.wikisource Kant Aufklärung, and Greek Wikisource for Epictetus and Epicurus. Record Perseus URL patterns exactly (Republic needs book + page=NNN; Theaetetus text-key is 'Theaet.').

research.summary: Partial result. Project Gutenberg (Finnish) has several early Plato translations: Gorgias (Forsman, 1899), Pidot/Symposion (Lehmuskoski, WSOY 1919), Faidoni (J. W. Calamnius). No Finnish Kant, Aristotle, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius or Snellman turned up there. I could not read the consolidated tekijänoikeuslaki 22 § on Finlex, because the site loads by JavaScript. Every claim below comes from search snippets, not from a page I read, so no claim reaches 'verified'. The Gutenberg ebook pages returned 503 on both fetches.

findings.claim: Gutenberg hosts Finnish 'Gorgias', Helsinki 1899, Suomalaisen Kirjallisuuden Seura, translator K. Forsman. The preface is signed April 1899 in Hämeenlinna and calls it the first volume of the 'Filosoofinen kirjasto' series, with Plato's Valtio announced next.

Translator identity for Gorgias: the Gutenberg record names Forsman, Kaarlo, 1851-1918. A second record lists 'Koskimies, Kaarlo, 1851-1918', probably a metadata mismatch. Death year 1918 is likely, so the work is public domain in Finland (70 years end 1988). The two names should be resolved against the book's title page or the Finnish national bibliography.

Gutenberg hosts 'Pidot (Symposion)', translated by Niilo Lehmuskoski (1888-1948), citing a WSOY Porvoo 1919 edition. Plato's Phaidros (Lehmuskoski, 1920) is also reported. Lehmuskoski died in 1948, so the 70-year term ended after 2018. This is a recent public-domain case and should be checked against the edition's title page before use.

Gutenberg hosts 'Faidoni' (Plato) translated by J. W. Calamnius, released 8 Sep 2006. The first Finnish Plato translation was Faidon in the early 1880s, per Niiniluoto. Whether the Gutenberg text is that 1880s translation, and Calamnius's death year, were not checked, so public-domain status is unverified.
No Gutenberg Finnish edition of Plato's Valtio (Republic) or the Apology was found. The Kansalliskirjasto authority record exists for a Finnish Valtio, but its translator and year were not read.

No Finnish Kant, Aristotle, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius or Snellman titles were found on Gutenberg in a search of the Gutenberg indexes. Doria, Digi and Internet Archive were not searched, so absence there is not shown. Snellman wrote in Swedish and Finnish and died in 1881, so his originals are public domain.

Tekijänoikeuslaki 22 § (quotation right): from a work already made public, one may quote 'hyvän tavan mukaisesti' and to the extent the purpose requires. The source is a search snippet and the Tekijänoikeusneuvosto's 2015 opinion, not the Finlex page. The attribution duty (name and source, 11 §) is not confirmed from a page I read.

A translator holds copyright in the translation if it passes the originality threshold, and this does not limit the original author's rights. The 1995 government proposal (HE 8/1995) describes extension of the term from 50 to 70 years after the author's death. The current term is 70 years from the author's death (43 §), and a translation's term should run from the translator's death. These claims come from snippets, with no direct statement of the translation term.

Finlex consolidated law 404/1961 returned only navigation text on all tries. One PDF at finlex.fi/api/media/statute/9863 turned out to be a 2023 amending act (HE 313/2022 and related), not the consolidated text. 22 § and 11 § text was not obtained.

Checking a translation (back-translation, a second reader of the source language) and the label 'suomennos: sivusto' with passage references: no source was read. This is project-rule practice (CLAUDE.md rule 5) and general scholarly convention, not a verified external claim.

recommendations: Before the build, read 404/1961 22 §, 11 § and 43 § from a text-extractable source (the Finlex open data XML/AKN, or the edilex or WIPO Lex texts) so the quotation and term rules are verified.

Use own translations ('suomennos: sivusto') as the default. Treat the Gutenberg Plato items as optional named quotations, only after checking each translator's death year and the title page. The Forsman 1899 Gorgias is the safest. The Lehmuskoski items (d. 1948) are later and need the death year confirmed.
Search Kansalliskirjasto Digi, Doria and Finna for Finnish Kant, Snellman and Aristotle translations. This pass did not cover them.

Label every own translation with author, work, passage reference (Stephanus, Bekker, or book and section), source URL, read date, and 'suomennos: sivusto'. Add the name of the checker, and the second reader of the source language where one exists.
Check each translation by back-translation, then have a second reader of the source language, and keep the check recorded. Per the project rule, the checker must not be the translator.

research.summary: The filosofia exam is 120 points. Part 1 has six 20-point tasks and the candidate answers 3-5 of them. Part 2 has three 30-point tasks and the candidate answers 0-2. A full score needs 3 Part 1 and 2 Part 2 tasks, and 5 tasks is the maximum. Every task is graded as one holistic score per task section (tehtäväosio), judged on osuvuus (relevance, the most important), eheys (coherence) and vakuuttavuus (persuasiveness). Sections worth 10 p or more are essays unless the task says otherwise. Sections of 10 p or less carry a character cap (a capped essay at 10 p). The same task shapes recur across 2024-2026: short concept definitions (4-5 p each, 600/750 characters), a 20-item multiple-choice or matching block worth 1-2 p per item, essays with or without material, a choose-two-of-four method task (3, 2026), and 30-p tasks split into sub-parts of 5/10/15/20 p. Materials in recent exams are texts, video and audio (lyrics plus recording), and the exam is done on a computer. The exam is mapped to LOPS19 modules inside each task's grading text. In LOPS19 the fourth module FI4 is 'Totuus', not 'Tieto, tiede ja todellisuus' as the brief's expected answer says. I read the grading instructions for five sittings (spring 2024, autumn 2024, spring 2025, autumn 2025, spring 2026) plus the autumn 2026 PDF. I could not read any 2023 sitting (spring or autumn).

findings.claim: Exam structure, spring 2025: nine tasks, answer five, 120 p. Part 1 is six 20-p tasks (answer 3-5), Part 2 is three 30-p tasks (answer 0-2). Full marks need 3 Part 1 and 2 Part 2 tasks. The same structure applies in spring 2024 and spring 2026.

Autumn 2025 structure is the same. Part 1: 1 Sivistys ja filosofia (essay on Toppinen text 1.A, material use required); 2 five 4-p concept definitions at max 600 characters (anarchism, democracy, Hume's guillotine, categorical imperative, moral agent); 3 Vapaa tahto (essay, no material); 4 Tuiskun valinta (essay, text 4.A required, apply at least one normative theory); 5 Valtio (compare two social-philosophy theories); 6 Historianfilosofia (text 6.A plus own history studies). Part 2: 7 Looginen argumentaatio (3+6+6+15 p, 450/750-character limits for the short parts); 8 Ihmis- ja perusoikeudet (two 15-p essays, texts 8.A-C); 9 Tieteen etiikka (10+5+15 p, texts 9.A-B).

Spring 2025 tasks: 1 philosophical questions (essay); 2 the trolley problem (essay); 3 everyday knowledge (essay); 4 descriptive and normative claims in moral relativism (video 4.A); 5 social-philosophy concepts, four 5-p parts of max 750 characters; 6 ten matching items of 2 p (pick the term from a dropdown of 20). Part 2: 7 Epictetus (two 15-p essays, texts and video); 8 Hobbes (20 p + 10 p, text 8.A); 9 necessary and sufficient conditions (5+5 short answers, 20-p essay on family resemblance, text 9.A).

Autumn 2024 tasks: 1 twenty statements from different branches of philosophy (1 p per correct); 2 life philosophies (essay); 3 argument evaluation (identify and assess arguments, essay form not required, discussion material 3.A); 4 forbidden acts (four 5-p parts, 750 characters); 5 justification of wealth and welfare differences (compare two theories); 6 Wittgenstein's philosophy of language (video optional). Part 2: 7 philosophy's contribution today (10+20 p, materials 7.A-B); 8 abortion, ethics and society (5+5+10+10 p, material 8.A); 9 scientific realism vs empiricist antirealism (15+15 p, interview 9.A, van Fraassen).

Spring 2026 (25.3.2026) tasks: 1 five 4-p definitions at max 600 characters (subjective, information, empirical, necessary truth, materialism); 2 moral relativism (essay); 3 philosophical methods (two of four methods, 10 p each, max 1,500 characters); 4 robots and morality (Chinese-room style); 5 freedom, equality and privilege (lyrics 5.A plus audio 5.B); 6 twenty multiple-choice items of 1 p with an 'En vastaa' opt-out. Part 2: 7 absolute truth (15+15 p, video 7.A); 8 research-based knowledge and political decision-making (15+15 p, Railo text 8.A); 9 epistemic injustice (5+5 short parts of max 750 characters plus a 20-p essay, Fricker video 9.A).

Autumn 2026 (22.9.2026) tasks: 1 fallacies (five 4-p explanations with an example, max 600 characters); 2 normative-ethics theories (essay describing two theories); 3 empirical scientific knowledge (essay); 4 offensive and discriminatory speech (essay, material required); 5 twenty multiple-choice statements on social philosophy, 1 p each; 6 alternative facts (essay, material). Part 2: 7 ethical diet (5+5 short parts, 750 characters, plus an essay with material); 8 endangered democracy (an essay, plus 8.2 as a 10-p capped essay of 1,500 characters); 9 truthlikeness (15+15 p, material 9.A). The exam is graded on preliminary good-answer criteria.

Grading framework (identical wording in the 2024-2026 pages I read): the three dimensions are each scored at 0/25/50/75/100%, and the holistic result is one score per task section. Sections of 10 p or more have three anchor points (about 25-30%, 50-60%, 75-80%) and sections of 5 p have two (40% and 80%). Essay form is introduction with problem or thesis, versatile body, conclusions based on the body. Required material not used: at least 1 p deducted and a cap of 75% of the section maximum. Optional ('voit hyödyntää') material can be ignored without penalty. Exceeding a character limit gives a deduction and falling short is not penalised. Irrelevant material lowers the value of the answer. Bloom levels are not to be applied as a rigid hierarchy. Writing quality counts only as far as it shows good philosophical thinking.

Per-task scoring guidance in YTL's good-answer features gives point anchors. Example (autumn 2025, 20-p essay): about 5 p for scattered remarks, 10 p for the required task element done, 15 p for coherent, varied reasoning, and top marks for deeper discussion of a named issue. Short parts: 2 p for correct-direction remarks, 4 p for a precise, clear explanation, and an example alone earns at most 2 p. Multi-part 30-p tasks use 4/8/12 anchors for 15-p parts.

OPH essay guidance: relevance is the most important of the three criteria; tasks of 10 p or more need essay form; a relevant, well-structured answer earns about half the points; no fixed word count; source-based tasks need own words with quotations marked and charitable interpretation. The page also has an eight-statement self-assessment rated 1-5.

The LOPS19 module names used in YTL's task mappings are FI1 Johdatus filosofiseen ajatteluun, FI2 Etiikka, FI3 Yhteiskuntafilosofia, and FI4 Totuus. The brief's expected answer names FI4 'Tieto, tiede ja todellisuus', which is wrong against YTL's wording.

YTL's page on publishing exam tasks says the board treats exam questions as official written statements without copyright. research.summary: The image budget is easy and the plan fits. The two sibling sites have spent about $0.96 of the $10 grant: $0.553 on opinto-ohjaus (12 nano-banana at $0.0336 plus 30 p-image at $0.005) and $0.405 on terveystieto (81 p-image at $0.005), so about $9.04 is left. A first-module plan of 18 new images costs about $0.60 to make once and about $0.90 with a 50% redo allowance. The whole four-module site comes to about $2.5 to $3. Wikimedia Commons has public-domain files, with licence data, for School of Athens, Death of Socrates, Descartes, Hume, Kant and Wollstonecraft, and for Plato's cave in Saenredam's engraving. The licence is public-domain by age, which is the same on every file. One caution: the Finnish photograph right (Copyright Act 49a) is a possible reproduction risk, so keep it as a documented decision rather than a given.

findings.claim: Spend so far from the run logs: opinto-ohjaus data/images.run.yaml has 12 google/nano-banana-2.1 entries at $0.0336 and 30 prunaai/p-image at $0.005 ($0.553). Terveystieto's log has 81 p-image entries at $0.005 ($0.405). Total about $0.96 of the $10 grant, so about $9.04 left. The brief's 'about $9 left' matches. The terveystieto 012 judgement notes that the log has 20 duplicate lines, so true spend may be slightly lower.

The engine's nano-banana adapter is model id google/nano-banana-2.1 at 0.0336 USD, and nano-banana takes no seed (the log records null). Allowed manifest models are nano-banana, klein and p-image. Output is webp under 195 KB. The command is 'lukio-runko images' with --max-dollars (default 10), a dry-run plan printed first, and GAME_ENGINE_DIR required.

On opinto-ohjaus, nano-banana made all 7 Finnish text diagrams correctly on the first pass, with one remake of dg-opintojen-rakenne. The 3 and 7 judgements record all as accepted. The 12 nano entries are 8 diagrams (7 plus 1 remake) and 4 illustrations (il-op2 among them). p-image was chosen for illustrations only because klein failed on a full disk (D-009).

Lessons from sibling image rounds: p-image does not obey counts ('four scenes' became six, so put counts in diagrams). Redo rounds were needed for worried faces (te2-09), children who look 11 to 14 instead of 16 to 19 (te3-04), a style-mismatched textured picture (te1-04), malformed bicycles and objects, and alt text that no longer matched the picture. Short prompts shaped like the others worked best. The judges open pictures at full size and check that the alt matches.

Sibling style line (terveystieto data/images.yaml): calm flat editorial illustration, soft simple shapes, clean edges, muted teal, warm sand, pale sky blue, soft coral and deep slate on off-white, Nordic school-website feel, airy composition, fictional people only, absolutely no text, letters, numbers, signs, logos or watermarks, with screens and papers blank. Illustrations are decorative with alt empty (decorative: true), and diagrams carry the information. Mermaid renders flowcharts to SVG and Vega-Lite renders charts; image models do not draw diagrams (D-006).

Replicate's nano-banana page describes Google's Gemini 2.5 image model. It states that small faces and fine facial details may lack precision, text in images may have spelling errors, character consistency is not guaranteed, intricate details may need several iterations, and all outputs carry SynthID watermarking. The Replicate page gives no price or aspect-ratio list, so 0.0336 comes only from the engine adapter. Note: the Replicate page I read is google/nano-banana (2.5), while the engine uses nano-banana-2.1. Behaviour claims come from the 2.5 page and may be slightly outdated for 2.1.

Google's AI Studio image-generation docs recommend multi-turn iteration, a specific subject and setting, reference images (up to 10 object images on Nano Banana 2.1 and 3.1 Flash), and uppercase K sizes. Aspect ratios 16:9, 5:4, 1:1 and 4:3 appear in the examples. I read the first 100,000 of 241,078 characters, which gave no real-person policy and no price.

Which philosophy topics a picture helps: a picture helps where the scene IS the thought experiment (the cave, the ship of Theseus, the trolley problem, the veil of ignorance, Mary's room, the experience machine, Descartes' demon, plus Gyges' ring, the Chinese room and Hume's billiard balls). Pure argument structure (premises and conclusions, the branches of philosophy, ethical theories compared, the validity table) is better in Mermaid with Finnish labels, as on the sibling sites. Primary-text boxes get a Commons public-domain portrait or artwork rather than a generated picture. This is a design judgement, not a source fact.

Raphael's School of Athens: the full file 'The School of Athens by Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino.jpg' is 17402x12132 px (207 MB), LicenseShortName Public domain, artist Raphael, dated 1509-1511. The API listed no templates and the credit says 'Own work', so use a downscaled thumbnail of about 2000 px from Commons and credit it as a photo of the fresco. A smaller alternative is 'Sanzio 01 Plato Aristotle.jpg' (804x1052, a detail of Plato and Aristotle, 191 KB), with templates PD-old-100-expired and PD-Art, credit Web Gallery of Art, 1509. Other public-domain detail scans exist: 'School of Athens Raphael detail 01.jpg' (3000x2251), 'detail 02' (2250x3000) and 'detail 03' (3000x2008). A Heraclitus detail 1460x1776 is also in the search results.

David, Death of Socrates (1787): 'Jacques-Louis David - The Death of Socrates (Google Art Project).jpg', 4000x2653 px, 4.3 MB, LicenseShortName Public domain, templates PD-old-100-expired, PD-Art (PD-old-auto-expired) and CC-PD-Mark. Credit is Google Arts & Culture. The painting shows hemlock and a death scene, so under the safe-messaging rules use it for the Socrates trial and philosophical method, not for an ethics-of-death page.

Descartes: 'Frans Hals - Portret van René Descartes.jpg', 817x1000 px, 155 KB, LicenseShortName Public domain, dated 1649, artist 'After Frans Hals'. The API showed Artwork and Cc-pd-mark-footer but did not list PD-old-100 or PD-Art as a template for this file (an earlier partial query had suggested them). The credit is a 1997 book scan (De eeuw van Rembrandt). The portrait is a copy after Hals, the source scan is of a book reproduction, and the resolution is low. Check the live file page before committing it.

Hume: 'Allan Ramsay - David Hume, 1711 - 1776 (Google Art Project).jpg', 3365x4001 px, 3.6 MB, Public domain, painted 1766, templates PD-old-100-expired, PD-Art and CC-PD-Mark, credit Google Cultural Institute.

Kant: 'Immanuel Kant - Gemaelde 1.jpg', 1009x1317 px, 665 KB, Public domain, artist Johann Gottlieb Becker (1720-1782), dated 1768. The API listed no licence template and the source is an archived andreasvieth.de page, so the licence is public-domain by age (the painter died in 1782). The file's stated source is a private website, so check the page for the exact tag. The names I guessed for a Tischbein Kant and an Opie Google Art file do not exist on Commons.

Wollstonecraft: 'Mary Wollstonecraft by John Opie (c. 1797).jpg', 1020x1244 px, 326 KB, Public domain, templates PD-Art, PD-old-auto-expired and others, artist John Opie (1761-1807). Larger alternatives: 'Mary Wollstonecraft Tate portrait.jpg' (1263x1536), 'Mary Wollstonecraft Portrait.jpg' (1634x1970) and 'Mary Wollstonecraft by John Opie from the National Portrait Gallery.jpg' (1272x1536), all listed as Public domain with artist John Opie. The page carries a third-party copyright-claim notice, which is not a source credit.

Plato's cave: 'Platon Cave Sanraedam 1604.jpg', 1600x1166 px, 2.4 MB, Public domain, credit British Museum, artist Jan Saenredam after Cornelis van Haarlem, 1604. The API listed Cc-pd-mark-footer but no PD-Art or PD-old template. A mirror says the Commons page also needs a US public-domain tag. NGA calls its own copy open access. Use the Commons or British Museum copy, and not the Ashmolean copy, which is CC BY-NC-ND. A real engraving of the cave is a useful alternative or addition to a generated image.

Rousseau (La Tour, c. 1750): 'Jean-Jacques Rousseau (painted portrait).jpg', 1448x2016 px, 1.5 MB, Public domain, templates PD-Art, PD-old-auto-expired and PD-old-X-expired, credit 'Unknown source'. It is licence-fine but poorly sourced, so confirm provenance before use.

The licence status of these paintings comes from the artists' death years (all more than 70, mostly more than 100, years ago), which are already shown on Commons. Photographs of 2D PD artworks: the Commons PD-Art guide says Nordic countries, citing Article 49a of the Finnish Copyright Act, give a 50-year photograph right, and that since 2021 the right in photos of 2D art lasts only while the artwork is protected (EU Directive 2019/790 Article 14). The page does not state how Finland transposed Article 14, so I treat the Finnish position on faithful reproductions as likely free but not fully settled. A file that was a photograph taken before 1976 or published before 1966 is fine under any reading. Safest rule: prefer scans where the photographer is not a claimant, record the Commons page URL, uploader credit and licence tag in the manifest, and let the operator decide on the residual risk.

Cost estimate for a first-module (FI1) image plan, assuming about 9 topics, all at $0.0336: 1 front-page hero, 1 module header, 9 topic headers and 7 thought-experiment illustrations (cave, ship of Theseus, Descartes' demon, trolley problem, veil of ignorance, Mary's room, experience machine, or whichever FI1 content needs) is 18 images, $0.60. With a 50% redo allowance, 27 calls, about $0.91. Public-domain artworks cost $0. If p-image were used for headers at $0.005, 11 headers would save about $0.31 but the style would vary. The whole four-module site at about 60 images with redos is about $2.5 to $3. This is far under the €5 operator-approval threshold in CLAUDE.md.

Rules proposed. 1) No real-person likeness is ever requested from the model (no named philosopher or political figure), and portraits come from public-domain Commons files with attribution. 2) No text, letters, numbers or signs in any picture, and anything with words is Mermaid or SVG. 3) Religion: no depiction of God, prophets or sacred figures and no mockery. Descartes' demon is drawn as an abstract shadow, a puppeteer's strings or a mist, not a devil. 4) Trolley and Socrates: no injured, bleeding or dying people, so the trolley is a toy tram with pegs on a fork track, and the hemlock scene is not used on ethics pages. 5) Hands and faces: keep figures small, in silhouette or from behind, since the nano page warns of fine facial detail; this is also the sibling lesson about worried faces and ages. 6) Students about 16 to 19, never uniforms. 7) One scene per prompt, no counts. 8) Decorative pictures use alt empty, and informative ones use a full Finnish alt that matches the final picture. 9) Every generated image is logged in images.run.yaml, with SynthID marks left intact.

Style line proposed for philosophy (a variant of the sibling one): 'Calm, thoughtful flat editorial illustration with soft simple shapes and clean edges, soft limited palette of deep indigo, warm sand, pale sky blue, muted gold and soft coral on an off-white background, airy and quiet like a Nordic school website; small stylised figures, often seen from behind or in silhouette; a hint of classical or everyday setting; fictional people only; absolutely no text, letters, numbers, signs, logos or watermarks; any books, screens and walls are blank or show only abstract shapes; no weapons, blood, injuries, religious figures or symbols.' The palette change gives the site its own identity while keeping the same flat look that judges accepted.

recommendations: Use nano-banana (google/nano-banana-2.1 at $0.0336) for every new picture. At this price the whole site stays under about $3 even with 50% redos, so p-image is only a fallback if the engine call fails. Set --max-dollars 2 per brief.

Draw the thought experiments as one calm scene each, with no text and small figures from behind: cave (figures facing a blank wall with shadow shapes), ship (a boat on a slipway with fresh and old planks), Descartes' demon (a figure beneath an abstract shadow with strings), trolley (a toy tram and wooden pegs on a fork), veil (figures at a round table behind a translucent curtain), Mary's room (a grey room with a window onto a red apple), experience machine (a person asleep in a soft glowing pod in a bright room). Each prompt carries the style line and short negatives.
Use Mermaid for argument structure, the branches of philosophy and compared ethical theories, with Finnish labels checked as on the sibling sites. Do not ask nano-banana for diagrams or text.

Commit public-domain artworks locally under site-src/img with a manifest row: Commons file title, URL, artist and death year, licence tag, date read, and a Finnish credit line ('Kuva: Wikimedia Commons, julkinen omaisuus'). Use a thumbnail around 1600 to 2000 px, because the full School of Athens file is 207 MB and the engine caps images at 195 KB webp.

Before adding the Descartes (copy after Hals), Kant (private-site source) and Rousseau (unknown source) images, open each Commons page and confirm provenance and the PD tag. Hume (Google Art Project), Wollstonecraft (Opie, Tate or NPG copy), School of Athens and Death of Socrates are in the best-documented group.

Record the Finnish photograph-right question (Copyright Act 49a versus Directive 2019/790 Article 14) as a decision the operator can confirm. The default is faithful reproductions of 2D works of PD artists, from Commons with the page URL stored.

Add the human-reviewer step the siblings used: open every generated image at full size, since judges failed pictures only at that point (ages, worried faces, alt mismatch), and write the final alt after the picture exists.

Keep the images brief small: FI1 plan of about 18 images ($0.60 plus a redo allowance of about $0.30), then FI2 to FI4 in their own briefs. Reserve the Death of Socrates for the Socrates and method page.

research.summary: Read-only review of ../lukion-terveystieto (CLAUDE.md, content contract with all three addenda, style guide, subject.yaml, engine-issues E-1..E-13, the 10 diaries, one TE3 topic, module-content.js, pages.yml, image manifests) and the lukio-runko README plus engine source (checks.py, markdown_render.py, pictures.py, images.py, subject.py, fetch_curriculum.py). A filosofia site can reuse nearly everything structurally: engine formats, subject.yaml shape, the numeric-assessment exam sections, the 75/60/45 plan tables, the rubric-section workaround, the image pipeline, and the workflow skeleton (scout.js, module-content.js). The real changes are in the content layer. There is no primary-text box and no language tagging in the engine. The build's figure and link checks interact badly with passage references and Wikipedia/Wikisource URLs. Health-safety rules shrink to a sensitive-themes subset. The checker set must swap health-facts for source/translation/worldview checks. I tested three engine behaviours directly by running the engine's own code: the date regex hits chapter references such as 1.7; the link regex truncates URLs that contain parentheses; and a div block does not render Markdown inside it. All local-file findings are verified (read in this session). Nothing was fetched from the web, because this aspect is local-only. Nothing was edited.

proposal.title: FI2, FI3 and FI4 outline (topic titles and key classics; links to confirm in later briefs)
proposal.detail:
FI2 Etiikka (6 objectives / 6 content items):
(1) Moraali, laki ja tapa; relativismi ja objektivismi (s1). Classics: Herodotus III.38 (custom is king), Plato Euthyphro 10a.
(2) Kuvaileva ja normatiivinen; Humen giljotiini (t2). Hume, Treatise 3.1.1 (PD).
(3) Hyve-etiikka. Aristotle, NE I 1098a and II 1106b (Bekker).
(4) Seurausetiikka. Bentham, IPML ch. I (1789); Mill, Utilitarianism ch. II (1863).
(5) Velvollisuusetiikka. Kant, Grundlegung AA IV 421 and 429 (Kirchmann scan on the Internet Archive, verified by the researcher).
(6) Oikeudet ja ihmisoikeudet (s6). Locke, Second Treatise ch. II; Wollstonecraft, Vindication; the UDHR as a linked document.
(7) Hyvä ja merkityksellinen elämä (s3). Epicurus, Ad Menoeceum (DL X 122-135, el.wikisource verified); Epictetus; Seneca, De brevitate vitae.
(8) Omat moraaliset ratkaisut: ihmissuhteet ja elämänvalinnat (s4). Aristotle, NE VIII-IX on friendship; Kierkegaard (Danish, d. 1855) optional.
(9) Eläimet, luonto ja ilmasto (s5). Bentham, IPML XVII footnote ('Can they suffer?'); modern authors link-out only.
Sensitive themes: euthanasia and suicide in ethics get safe-messaging pages.

FI3 Yhteiskuntafilosofia (5/6):
(1) Yhteiskuntasopimus. Hobbes, Leviathan XIII-XIV (1651 Head edition, en.wikisource verified); Locke, Second Treatise VIII; Rousseau, Du contrat social I.6 (fr.wikisource 1762, URL to confirm).
(2) Valta ja vapaus. Mill, On Liberty I (harm principle, 1859); Machiavelli, Il Principe XVIII optional.
(3) Tasa-arvo ja oikeudenmukaisuus. Plato, Republic I-II (Thrasymachus, Gyges 359c); Aristotle, Politics III; Wollstonecraft. Rawls (not PD) is paraphrase and link-out.
(4) Oikeusvaltio, demokratia ja yhteisö. Aristotle, Politics III.
(5) Poliittiset ihanteet. Mill (liberalism); Marx and Engels, Manifest 1848 (socialism); Burke, Reflections 1790 (conservatism); Kropotkin (anarchism, d. 1921); Snellman (nationalism, Swedish and Finnish, d. 1881); More, Utopia 1516 (Latin) for utopias.
(6) Hyvinvointi, talous ja ajankohtaiset kysymykset (technology and AI, gender and power). No PD classic is needed; Beauvoir is not PD and is link-out only.
Safe messaging applies to political violence.

FI4 Totuus (6/7):
(1) Kieli, merkitys ja totuus. Frege, Über Sinn und Bedeutung 1892 (d. 1925, PD); Wittgenstein, Tractatus (German original only, once a text is confirmed).
(2) Totuusteoriat. Aristotle, Met. 1011b (correspondence); James, Pragmatism 1907 (d. 1910); coherence theory in paraphrase.
(3) Välttämätön ja kontingentti. Leibniz, Monadologie 33 (French, d. 1716).
(4) Todellisuus ja tietoisuus; realismi ja antirealismi. Berkeley, Principles 1710; Plato's cave reused.
(5) Tiedon lähteet ja rajat. Locke, Essay II.1; Descartes, Med. I; Kant, KrV B1 (Akademie edition).
(6) Tieteellinen päättely ja tieteen etiikka. Bacon, Novum Organum I (Latin, 1620); Hume on induction; Popper link-out.
(7) Selittäminen ja ymmärtäminen. Dilthey (d. 1911) optional; von Wright (not PD) is link-out.
Van Fraassen (2024 exam) is link-out.

Counts for planning: FI2 about 9 topics, FI3 about 8, FI4 about 9.

proposal.title: Translation plan
proposal.detail:
1. DEFAULT: the site's own Finnish translation from the PD original, labelled 'suomennos: sivusto'. A PD Finnish translation is used only after the translator's death year (died before 1956) and the title page are read and recorded; candidates are Forsman's Gorgias 1899 and Lehmuskoski's Symposion 1919 and Phaidros 1920, all unverified now.

2. LENGTH: 1-4 sentences per quotation and at most 2-3 primary-text boxes per topic (500-line cap). Quote the original in the box too, as the original is PD.

3. BOX FIELDS, in order: label 'Lähdeteksti'; the original in a blockquote with <span lang="grc|la|de|fr|en">; the Finnish in a second blockquote ending 'suomennos: sivusto'; a reference line with author, work, the traditional reference (Stephanus 'Apologia 38a'; Bekker 'Metafysiikka 1011b25'; AT 'AT VII 25'; 'Encheiridion 1'; 'DL X 122'; 'Tutkimus inhimillisestä ymmärryksestä, jakso IV'), the edition named on the page (Burnet 1903; Ross 1924; Adam-Tannery; Berlinische Monatsschrift 1784; Hume 1748 Millar), the open URL and the read date. Never write N.N book.chapter forms in running text (the engine's date scanner flags them); use 'kirja 1, luku 7', roman numerals, or Stephanus or Bekker forms.

4. CHECKING: a second agent (Opus, as CLAUDE.md requires for translation review) who did not translate opens the cited edition page and confirms: the passage exists at that reference, the translation is faithful (back-translation into English plus a list of the choices made), and the reference and URL match. Record checker, date and verdict in the topic's front matter or a data/translations.yaml row: id, topic, author, work, ref, edition, url, read, translator: sivusto, checked_by, checked_on, status. Recommend a human reader of the source language before publishing. A judge's request to change a translation also goes through this checker.

5. NEVER COPY: modern Finnish translations (for example the Otava Plato, the Gaudeamus Kant, any translator alive or died after 1955); Loeb English shown by default on Perseus (Tredennick 1933/1989 and others; Fowler and Lamb may be PD in the EU but are not the source text, so do not use them); Ogden's Tractatus (EU PD only from 2028); OPH, Logos, SEP, IEP or Yle prose; YTL tasks or their materials. Modern translations may be named as reading tips (title, translator, publisher) without quoting. Paraphrase only non-PD authors (Popper, Russell, Rawls, Beauvoir, Fricker, van Fraassen).

6. LAW: the quotation right (22 §: proper usage, extent the purpose requires) and the source duty (11 §) are verified on the WIPO 1997 text. Re-read the current 22 § (amended 2015) before the contract cites the law itself. PD status uses 43 §: the end of the 70th year after death.

- Pin lukio-runko v0.1.0 and set TZ Europe/Helsinki in pages.yml.

CONTRACT ADDITIONS on top of terveystieto's:

(A) Primary-text box ('Lähdeteksti'). A bold label line, then a blockquote with the original in <span lang="xx">, a second blockquote with the Finnish plus 'suomennos: sivusto' (or a named PD translator and year), and a reference line (author, work, traditional reference, edition, link, read date). No <div> wrappers: the engine does not render Markdown inside them. Every box URL is also in official_links. Percent-encode parentheses in URLs. No N.N citation forms. At most 3 boxes per topic. A box must be passage-checked by the sources checker. Log engine issues E-14 onward: no box styling, html lang fixed to fi, the date scanner hits citations, the link regex breaks on parentheses, 'Apua ja tukea' is mandatory everywhere.

(B) Exam formats, mirroring YTL shapes with no A/B/C parts. Headings stay '### K1: Nimi, N min (20 p)'. Types (slugs):
- maarittele-ja-esimerkki: 5 x 4 p, 600 characters.
- monivalinta: 20 x 1 p, with the 'En vastaa' option.
- kasite-essee: 20 p, no material.
- aineisto-essee: 20 p, required material; at least 1 p deduction and a 75% cap if unused.
- menetelmatehtava: 2 of 4 x 10 p, 1,500 characters.
- argumentin-analyysi.
- kahden-teorian-vertailu.
- ajatuskoe-arviointi.
- 30 p multipart: 5+5+20, 15+15, 10+20, or 3+6+6+15; parts under 10 p get a 750-character cap.
Model answers carry a scoring guide on osuvuus (the most important), eheys and vakuuttavuus, banded 0/25/50/75/100%, with anchors 5/10/15 (20 p), 2/4 (5 p) and 4/8/12 (15 p), plus the fixed line 'Pisteytys on sivuston oma harjoitusohje, ei ylioppilastutkintolautakunnan.' The rubric lives as a section of opetussuunnitelma.md (E-11). Material is self-written and labelled 'kuvitteellinen', or a PD original excerpt with its own translation and reference. Never a past YTL task or attachment, reworded or not. At most one exam task per topic unless a brief asks.

(C) Worldview respect: present arguments with their strongest critics; no mockery of religious or non-religious views; no political advocacy; tasks ask to analyse and argue, never to adopt a view. Never assess the student's own beliefs. In model answers, 'both sides' must not make required curriculum content look optional.

(D) Sensitive themes (death, suicide in ethics, euthanasia, political violence, the Socrates death scene): safety_flags {death_suicide, violence}, a content_note meta row (E-2), an 'Apua ja tukea' section with youth services, no methods, no personal-disclosure prompts. The David painting stays off ethics-of-death pages. The health rules (figure scanner, privacy linter, medical advice) are dropped; ordinary pages keep a short 'Apua ja tukea' (study-help line) because the engine demands the section.

(E) Checkers: sources-and-translations (opens each edition page, confirms passage and translation, never the translator) and worldview-and-neutrality replace terveystieto's facts and safety checkers. The curriculum and pedagogy checkers stay. A front-matter key check runs after every fix round. The data owner joins every fix round.

(F) Front matter: required keys include school_adapts and accessibility (the engine needs them). Add primary_texts[] {author, work, ref, edition, url, read, lang, translation: sivusto|<translator year>, checked_by} and linked_materials with licence_class (E-3/E-4 workaround: also listed in official_links).

Reviewers: a filosofia teacher (curriculum, exam tasks, scoring guides); readers of Greek, Latin and German for the translations.
